name: Global-cap Bogle DCA
thesis: Buy and hold low-cost total-market index funds, adding on a schedule and never selling to time the market. Use each scheduled buy to steer toward a global market-cap mix (US ~60-65%, ex-US ~35-40%), because US cap-weighted indexes are now unusually concentrated in a few AI megacaps.
regimeFit: Same behavior in every regime: scheduled DCA. High rates or volatility only change where the next dollar goes (the most underweight fund), never whether to sell.
entryRules: One DCA ticket per trading day at the midday session, into the most underweight fund vs target (VTI 45%, VOO 15%, VXUS 35%, cash 5%).
Skip the ticket only if it would push cash below $10.
exitRules: No discretionary sells. Rebalancing sells need an explicit --override-reason and only when a fund drifts > 15 points from target.
sizingRules: Ticket ≈ $10 (or 50% of excess cash above $10, whichever is smaller).
Max 1 order per day; minimum ticket $5.
riskRules: Behavioral rule: news, rates and AI headlines are logged as context but cannot trigger sells.
Fractional ETF fills are modeled; real brokers may require whole shares.
personaConstraints: PAPER ONLY: no brokerage connection, no real orders.
Every order needs a same-day research record with X, web and market sources, a selected idea, a rationale and a confidence score (enforced by scripts/paper-order.mjs).
Fills: latest Yahoo quote (may lag ~15 min) ± 5 bps slippage; Schwab $0 commission; SEC Section 31 + FINRA TAF on sells.
Minimum ticket $5. Regular market hours only.

history.change: Initial research-driven strategy (replaces the deterministic rule plugin in simEngine.js).
history.reason: The user asked traders to research daily (X, web, SEC, market data) and choose strategies that fit conditions instead of following fixed rules blindly. Rules come from the persona profile plus the Oct 9 pre-market research.
